policy.rule: Before adding a custom parser, validator or storage layer, review at least one mature permissively licensed upstream candidate and record the decision here.

candidates.reason: Canonical static GTFS validator. Use as an external validation gate at meaningful release/data-ingest checkpoints; do not embed in browser/shared-host runtime.
Mature GTFS-RT rule set and batch processor. Keep outside request path; use selectively for diagnostics/staging because upstream still describes the project as early alpha.

Official generated GTFS-RT bindings are the preferred replacement candidate if U.Venice gains a bundler or Node service. Current browser-native decoder stays because adding protobufjs/Node-oriented bindings would materially enlarge the static runtime for a small field subset.

Excellent import/query stack, but its database/runtime model conflicts with the current static browser + Python stdlib builder + shared-host deployment. Re-evaluate if a persistent Node/database backend is introduced.
Already used as a permissively licensed architectural pattern for immutable incoming feed updates versus derived current-state snapshots; no Elixir dependency is bundled.
Existing MotionState logic selectively adapts schedule-deviation interpolation ideas without introducing the Java runtime.
OperationalModel follows TODS 2.1.0 concepts and field semantics while keeping an independent provider-neutral implementation.
Permissively licensed Italian rail GTFS producer. Reused as reference for GTFS output invariants such as >24h times, ordered stop_times and producer-side validation; no Go runtime is bundled.
Maps the same CCISS/Italian NeTEx feed and documents key entity relationships, but no explicit software license is present; used only to cross-check mappings, not as copied source.
Mature general converter and useful architecture reference, but not embedded in U.Venice due license/runtime/profile mismatch.
Repository contains an MIT LICENSE but README states it builds on Entur and is licensed under the same terms as the original Java implementation; provenance is ambiguous, so code is not copied.

custom_components.reason: Minimal browser decoder only handles fields used by U.Venice and keeps zero runtime dependencies. Replace with official bindings if a browser bundler or Node transit service becomes part of the architecture.
Streaming Python-stdlib builder is tailored to shared hosting and immutable runtime chunks. Canonical validator should validate inputs at release/ingest gates instead of replacing the builder.
Bounded sampled raw protobuf archive must run in existing PHP shared hosting with no database. Database/Elixir stacks are disproportionate for six-hour diagnostic retention.
Short-lived in-memory normalized history is intentionally bounded and browser-local; persistent database semantics are neither required nor desirable here.
Local check remains only a cheap structural preflight. It must not be treated as specification validation; canonical MobilityData validator is the preferred full validation gate.

Small Python-stdlib bridge targets only Italian NeTEx entities required by the existing runtime builder. It avoids AGPL/EUPL/ambiguous converter dependencies while reusing documented mapping and GTFS validation patterns.
